questions.title: What does the graph gradient mean?
questions.prompt: For the first captured source interval, check whether the supplied factors are known, then predict how interval-mean solar electrical power changes when irradiance increases by 100 W/m². Hold geometry, deployment and hardware fixed. Give the gradient with units, then explain a zero or unavailable result.
questions.hint: A gradient is output change divided by input change. A partial interval of deployment also scales interval-mean power.
questions.equation: P☉ = S A η (1 − ℓ) F☉ g
questions.symbols: S: irradiance (W/m²); A: collecting area (m²); η: conversion efficiency; ℓ: loss fraction; F☉: visible disk fraction; g: incidence factor. Fractions are dimensionless. For interval means include the fraction deployed.
context: Generation evidence for this interval is available. If collecting area, conversion efficiency or retained fraction is zero, the power response is zero even when a normalized collecting factor is undefined.

Use the combined fraction once: it already includes the share of this interval with deployed panels. Multiply it by area, conversion efficiency and retained fraction to obtain the gradient. If a required source factor is unavailable, state that limitation instead of inventing it.
questions.answer: The captured interval gradient ∂P̄☉/∂S is 1.02 m²; smooth sphere 1.02 m². A 100 W/m² increment produces 102 W. Units W ÷ (W/m²) = m². This is an irradiance response, not a time derivative. A zero can mean shadow, zero collecting efficiency or no active deployment; unavailable means the required evidence is missing.

questions.title: Will storage stay above the protected reserve?
questions.prompt: Calculate the protected energy floor, then the minimum margin above that floor during this stay. Does this one calculation establish landing readiness? Explain.
questions.hint: Multiply battery capacity by the reserve fraction. Subtract this floor from the full-stay minimum energy, including initial charge.
questions.symbols: The minimum margin is the lowest stored energy minus the protected fraction of battery capacity.
questions.answer: Protected floor = 2,000 Wh. Minimum margin = 8,000 Wh. A negative margin violates this reserve requirement. Zero is the boundary, not a safety allowance. This does not establish terrain safety, guidance, thermal survival, station allocation or mission approval.

questions.title: Why does a smooth Moon give a different answer?
questions.prompt: Compare generated energy with the measured-terrain horizon and the smooth sphere. Calculate their difference. Explain why moving a short distance can change the result without changing the solar panels.
questions.hint: Subtract sphere energy from terrain energy. A ridge can cover part or all of the low solar disk; effects depend on azimuth and date.
questions.symbols: Generated energy in the terrain and smooth-sphere cases is integrated over the same requested stay (Wh). The difference is a model comparison, not a new measurement.
questions.answer: Terrain minus sphere = 0 Wh. Local ridges change the horizon along the Sun’s path. Source cadence, prepared observer heights and terrain resolution limit what can be concluded. Do not infer unresolved boulders or touchdown hazards from this comparison.

questions.title: Can a visible Earth guarantee communications?
questions.prompt: Express geometric antenna contact as a percentage and compare the terrain result with the smooth sphere. Explain why a ground station may still be unusable during an interval with Earth visibility.
questions.hint: Multiply a known fraction by 100. Distinguish the lunar terrain/antenna mask from station visibility, radio margin, weather and booking.
questions.symbols: Contact fraction: share of the requested equal-duration source intervals clearing the stated lunar antenna cutoff (dimensionless). This is not delivered data volume or reserved station time.
questions.answer: Terrain 0 %; sphere 0 %. Geometric Earth visibility alone does not establish a complete link. Check dated station geometry, elevation/skyline, hardware and band, atmospheric attenuation, operating schedule, allocation, rates and critical windows. Unknown values remain unknown.
